content: {"rule": "K-S2", "applies": "no", "applies_why": "No; this judge text does not use a single verse's failure to state a link or contrary, nor does it treat a two-sense verse as open, as the ground for UNDERDETERMINED.", "verdict": "CLEAN", "quote": "D2 vs C1 (Matthew 1:20): UNDERDETERMINED -- the challenger's covenant-origin analogy is footed (1 Chronicles 28:6, Acts 1:8) but the sentence's own words state the source of what is in the womb; answered in [CR3] LINK 2.", "rule_words": "That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand.", "room": "A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand. I weighed applying this to the covenant-origin analogy versus the verse's own source statement, or not applying it because the analogy is footed by other verses while the verse itself states the source.", "why": "The judge cites a footed analogy from other verses against Matthew 1:20's own statement of the womb-source; it does not rest on a single verse's non-statement or on a two-sense verse being open."}
